article.story:
Aston Villa's hopes of earning automatic Champions League qualification took a blow after they were beaten 1-0 at Galatasaray on Tuesday.

Villa enjoyed a good start to the league phase, winning their first three games, but they followed up a 3-0 defeat at Barcelona with another reverse in Istanbul.

Deniz Gül's brave header in the 77th minute was enough to seal the win with the game's first shot on target.

With games against Paris Saint-Germain and Borussia Dortmund to come either side of Christmas, Unai Emery's men now have a challenge to finish in the top eight and earn a direct ticket into the knockout phase.

The loss makes it six games in all competitions without a win as Villa's rebuild takes time to bear consistent fruit.

The biggest concern was how they never looked like scoring, failing to register a shot on target throughout the 90 minutes.

The pre-match talk was about the state of the pitch at RAMS Park, with Galatasaray playing the weekend's league match away from the stadium in order for the surface to undergo emergency repairs.

As a result, Villa were unable to train on it ahead of the game and the pitch was plied with sand.

But the visitors initially acquitted themselves well and managed the cauldron of noise as they enjoyed a controlled start.

They looked lively going forward but struggled to create a clear sight of goal.

Their best moment came when they made a quick break down the right and the ball ended up with Johan Manzambi, but he could not get a shot away.

Galatasaray came into it as the first half progressed, but did not test Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, who will have welcomed a quiet opening after his recent troubles.

The intensity increased at the start of the second half and there were two flashpoints as tempers flared.

First, John McGinn and Aleksey Batrakov went into the book after McGinn flew into his counterpart as revenge for a heavy challenge on Alysson by former Tottenham defender Davinson Sánchez.

There was another coming together as João Gomes was booked for stopping Yunus Akgun's counter-attack.

The hosts suddenly had the bit between their teeth and they pushed Villa back.

They still could not test Suzuki as Aleksey Batrakov flashed a volley well over.

Villa looked to be shutting up shop and taking a point home, but they conceded in the 77th minute.

A loose ball from a corner fell to Gul, who showed bravery to head the ball home while taking a kick in the face from Nicolas Jackson.
